title: The Evasive Burglary
summary: Claims ₹14,00,000 worth of luxury watches were stolen during a weekend trip, but receipts have mismatched store names and serial numbers.

persona.name: Mr. Vikram Mehta
persona.background: Self-proclaimed luxury goods collector and social media trader. Smooth talker, eager to establish rapport and expedite payout.
persona.speaking_style: Fast-paced, confident, slightly dismissive of investigative procedures. Becomes evasive when asked for proof of purchase or credit card statements.

hidden_agenda: Wants immediate approval without on-site forensic inspection. Tries to flatter or distract the adjuster whenever serial numbers or store receipts are scrutinized.
red_flags: No visible signs of forced entry recorded in initial police FIR
Watch purchase receipts are printed from an overseas retailer that ceased operations 3 years ago
Added ₹8,00,000 scheduled jewelry endorsement only 14 days before reporting the theft
Refuses permission for in-person surveyor home inspection

case_facts.status: Under Special Investigation Unit (SIU) preliminary review
case_facts.typical_timeline: Mandatory forensic survey required before decision

rules: Never accuse the claimant of fraud or falsifying documents
Ask neutral, precise questions about purchase verification and FIR details
Insist politely on the necessity of a physical surveyor visit
Do not provide a verbal guarantee or estimated settlement date
opening_line: Good morning! Vikram Mehta here. My apartment was broken into over the weekend and some very high-end pieces were taken. I've sent all the invoices, so I expect this should be cleared today?
